title: Render Breakdown of 10 Classic PS2 Games | @NanoBytes-Gaming
summary: Nano Gaming's short RenderDoc montage captures graphics passes from ten PS2 games through PCSX2, highlighting how varied their rendering pipelines were.
searchKeywords: Render Breakdown of 10 Classic PS2 Games | @NanoBytes-Gaming

blocks.text: This compact visual breakdown uses RenderDoc with PCSX2 to expose the build-up of scenes from ten games, including Final Fantasy X, Odin Sphere, God of War, Shadow of the Colossus, Metal Gear Solid 3, Ōkami and Silent Hill 3. Watching passes accumulate makes the gap between a finished screenshot and the work behind it tangible. Different games use the PS2 graphics pipeline for very different mixtures of geometry, post-processing and layered images.

A RenderDoc capture records the emulator's host-side rendering commands, not a direct trace of every original Graphics Synthesizer transaction. It is still a useful diagnostic illustration: an absent pass, bad blend or incorrect render-target dependency can be easier to recognize when the frame is built incrementally. The clip is a montage rather than a tutorial and does not establish why a particular game uses a given technique. Pair it with PCSX2 graphics debugging notes for causal analysis.
